explanations: pollOnce only asks the queue for as many messages as it has free slots (concurrency minus inFlight). inFlight is decremented in the success callback, but the rejection callback only counts the failure and reports it. The message is correctly nacked, yet the slot is never given back. Each failed handler permanently uses up one slot, so after `concurrency` failures pollOnce always sees zero free slots and the consumer stops receiving, even though nothing is running. drain then reports a stall. Releasing the slot on both paths, here by decrementing inFlight in the error callback too (or by using .finally), keeps the worker pool at full capacity after failures.
